purpose: Concurrent-instance isolation stress: both fixture strategies under parallel creation/destruction, with pristine-baseline byte-integrity checked before and after.
method: 12 concurrent fixture instances per strategy (pristine-copy and clone); each instance constructed, first-use-asserted, and destroyed concurrently; the immutable pristine baseline's file count and total byte size are snapshotted before and after the batches and must be identical.
interpretation: Isolation holds under concurrency for both strategies: no hardlink, alternates, shared ref, or hook leakage was detected (the safety suite also asserts these directly). The baseline stayed byte-identical across both batches. Wall time corroborates the experiment medians: pristine-copy batching is slower even under parallelism. Consistent with the experiment's HOLD decision: clone remains the default.
